intro: This question helps us find the best place for you to begin.

widget.instructions: Press Play to launch the ball. Pause, step or scrub to follow its velocity arrow; the graphs show the horizontal and vertical parts separately.

stem: A ball is kicked from level ground at {{v}} m/s, {{ang}}° above the horizontal. Ignore air resistance and take g = 9.8 m/s².
How far away does it land?

hints.text: Treat the horizontal and vertical motions separately. Which one decides how long the ball is in the air? Watch the two graphs as the ball flies.
Time of flight: t = 2u sin θ ÷ g. Horizontal speed stays u cos θ.
Range = u cos θ × 2u sin θ ÷ g = u² sin 2θ ÷ g.

forgot-double-angle.text: The range uses sin 2θ, not sin θ: it comes from 2 sin θ cos θ, the time of flight times the horizontal speed.

used-time-to-apex.text: That's the distance covered while rising to the top: half the flight. The ball takes as long again to come down.

ignored-horizontal-component.text: Only the horizontal component u cos θ carries the ball sideways. The full speed u points partly upward.

dimension-mismatch.text: Range is a distance. Check your unit.

generic.text: Split the motion: the time in the air comes from the vertical part, the distance from the horizontal part. The coral flag marks your answer.

workedSolution.text: Horizontal speed: u cos θ = {{v}} cos {{ang}}° = {{vx}} m/s. It doesn't change.
Time of flight: t = 2u sin θ ÷ g = {{tf}} s.

forgot-double-angle.front: Range of a projectile on level ground?

used-time-to-apex.front: Is the time to the top the whole flight time?
used-time-to-apex.back: No, it's half of it (on level ground).

ignored-horizontal-component.front: Which velocity component carries a projectile sideways?
ignored-horizontal-component.back: The horizontal one, u cos θ, constant without air resistance.

generic.front: How do you find a projectile's range?
